newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli cabinet debate on budget cuts postponed.
newsitem.headline: Israeli cabinet debate on budget cuts postponed.

text.p: Israel's cabinet will hold a special meeting on the Treasury's proposed budget next week but not at its regular Sunday session, as previously announced, Treasury officials said on Thursday.

The Treasury is seeking reductions of between 500 million and 800 million shekels ($140.8-225.4 million) Approximately 180 million shekels of this is due to Israel's agreeing to transfer $50 million in U.S. foreign aid to Jordan, Treasury sources said.
They said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would be holding informal discussions with ministers before the meeting to enlist their support for the cuts.

This will market the third round of spending cuts to the 1997 budget in a bid to keep the deficit to the government's target of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product. To date the government has reduced spending or approved revenue-raising measures totalling seven billion shekels.
